extracted.intended_audience: users of SINGULAR and Normaliz (computational algebraists, mathematicians, and engineers using the normal.lib / normaliz.lib libraries)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in SINGULAR's normal.lib and normaliz.lib libraries: usage, return values, assumptions, notes and examples for functions that compute normalizations, invariants, conductors, closures, and related algebraic objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: HomJJ
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Endomorphism ring End_R(J)=Hom_R(J,J) with its ring structure as an affine ring, together with the canonical map R -> Hom_R(J,J), where R = P/id is the quotient ring of the basering P modulo the standard basis SBid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: HomJJ(Li) where Li = list: standard basis SBid, ideal id, ideal J, poly p with p a nonzero divisor of R. Returns list l: l[1] a polynomial ring containing ideals 'endid' and 'endphi' such that l[1]/endid = Hom_R(J,J) and 'endphi' describes the canonical map R -> Hom_R(J,J); l[2] = 1 if the canonical map phi is an isomorphism, 0 otherwise; l[3] = dim_K(Hom_R(J,J)/R) (contribution to delta) if finite, -1 otherwise. Note: printlevel >=1 displays comments. Example shown: definitions of ring, id, J, and invocation L = HomJJ(Li) and inspection of endid and psi (the map).

rubrics_metrics.name: genus
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the geometric genus p_g = p_a - delta of the projective curve defined by ideal i, treating projective curves (taking projective closure if input is affine 1-dim variety). Here delta is the sum of local delta-invariants (dim(R'/R), R' the normalization of the local ring R of each singularity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: genus(i) with optional flags: genus(I,"nor") uses normalization to compute delta (usually slower but sometimes not), genus(I,"pri") starts with a primary decomposition. Example given computing genus for two rings (characteristic 0 and 7) returning 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: primeClosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a chain of rings that lead to the integral closure (normalization) of a specified prime component: returns list L of rings L[1]..L[n] such that L[n]/ker is the integral closure of L[1]/ker in its quotient field; also returns L[n+1] as the delta invariant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: primeClosure(L [,c]) where L is a list of a ring containing a prime ideal ker; optional c selects the nonzero denominator (nzd) choice. Returned L: L[1] is a copy of input ring, rings L[i] contain ideals ker and phi giving injections L[1]/ker -> ... -> L[n]/ker; each L[i] contains a polynomial nzd so elements are quotients of previous ring via that denominator. Note: L is constructed by recursive calls to primeClosure; c not given or 0 chooses first generator of singular locus SL; c<>0 chooses generator with least number of monomials. Example provided showing ReesAlgebra and primeClosure producing ker generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: closureFrac
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the output list L (as from primeClosure) where L[n] contains an extra polynomial f, return a pair of elements (a fraction) from L[1] representing f via the injections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: closureFrac(L). Returns a list 'fraction' of two elements of L[1] such that f = fraction[1]/fraction[2] via the injections phi L[i]->L[i+1]. Example: normalizing R/ker and representing T(2) as x/y by closureFrac; demonstrates setring manipulations and use of phi and export.

rubrics_metrics.name: iMult
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the intersection multiplicity of a list of ideals L; if infinite, returns -1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: iMult(L) where L is a list of ideals. Theory: for r = 2, iMult(L)=vdim(std(L[1]+L[2])); in general iMult(L)=sum{iMult(L[j],Lj) | j=1..r-1} with Lj intersection of later ideals. Relation: if I is intersection of all ideals in L then delta(I)=delta(L[1])+...+delta(L[r])+iMult(L) where delta(I)=vdim(normalisation(R/I)/(R/I)). Examples given with numeric outputs (3 and 19).

rubrics_metrics.name: deltaLoc
rubrics_metrics.description: For a reduced bivariate polynomial f and an irreducible prime component J of its singular locus, compute sums of local invariants at the singular points described by J: delta invariants, Tjurina numbers, and numbers of branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: deltaLoc(f,J) with basering having exactly two variables and J one entry from minAssGTZ(I) for I = <f, jacob(f)>. Returns list L where L[1] = sum of local delta invariants at points given by J; L[2] = sum of local Tjurina numbers; L[3] = sum of local numbers of branches. Note: uses execute; increasing printlevel shows more comments. Example shows iterated calls deltaLoc(f,qr[i]) returning values for each singular component. See also references to delta and tjurina procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: locAtZero
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether a given ideal I (given as a standard basis) represents exactly one point located at zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: locAtZero(I). Returns 1 if I has only one point located at zero, 0 otherwise. Only useful in affine rings; in local rings vdim does the check. Example shows locAtZero returning 1 for a Jacobian ideal, and 0 after modifying the ideal to shift a point.

rubrics_metrics.name: norTest
rubrics_metrics.description: Test correctness/properties of a normalization computation 'nor' (output of normal, normalP("withRing"), or normalC): returns an intvec v describing injectivity, finiteness, and normality of the normalization map and ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: norTest(i,nor) (optionally norTest(i,nor,2) for partial test). Returns v with v[1]=1 if normap is injective else 0; v[2]=1 if normap is finite else 0; v[3]=1 if nor[1][1]/norid is normal else 0. If n=1 or 2 only first entries computed. Theory: basering/i -> nor[1][1]/norid is normalization iff v = 1,1,0 (note: doc says 'if and only if v=1,1,0' but examples show 1,1,1 for correct results). Note: for big examples full test may be hard; partial test norTest(i,nor,2) is usually fast. Example shows outputs and states '1,1,1 means normal was correct' for normal, normalC, and normalP outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: getSmallest
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the generator of ideal J of smallest degree (if multiple, choose the one with smallest number of monomials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: getSmallest(J). Note: looks only at the listed generators of J, not all polynomials in the ideal; intended mainly to compute a good universal denominator in normalization algorithms. Example shows selecting x2-y2+1 from generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: getOneVar
rubrics_metrics.description: From a 0-dimensional ideal J in a two-variable ring, return a polynomial in the specified variable (vari) of smallest degree that lies in J.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: getOneVar(J, vari). Works only over rings of two variables; intended as an auxiliary procedure for computing integral bases. Example: getOneVar(J,1) returning x9.

rubrics_metrics.name: changeDenominator
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ideals U1 and I and polynomials c1 and c2, compute an ideal U2 such that the A-modules (1/c1)*U1 and (1/c2)*U2 are equal, where A = R/I and R is the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: changeDenominator(U1, c1, c2, I). Returns ideal U2. Note: assumes such U2 exists; intended mainly as auxiliary procedure in normalization algorithms. Example demonstrates transforming normalization representation from denominator y^3 to x^3 producing U2 whose 1/x^3 * U2 equals normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalConductor
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the conductor of R/I as an ideal in R (i.e., the ideal of elements of R that map into the normalization), assuming I is radical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: normalConductor(I) (optional: normalConductor(I,L) if normalization already computed where L contains output of normal). The procedure uses minimal primes and generators from normalization algorithm. Examples: returning [1] (whole ring) if ring is normal (curveDeltaInv(I)=0), and specific generators for non-normal examples. See also curveConductorMult.

rubrics_metrics.name: normaliz library overview
rubrics_metrics.description: normaliz.lib provides an interface from SINGULAR to the external program Normaliz (>=2.11) for computations of integral closures, monoid/cone invariants, and related numerical invariants; data exchange is via files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prerequisite: Normaliz must be installed and executables in search path or set via setNmzExecPath. The library supports grading via intvec that assigns degrees to variables (generators must have positive degree). Data exchange files are created/erased automatically in automatic mode; for advanced use user can specify filenames and manage files. Numerical invariants computed by Normaliz can be accessed from SINGULAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: intclToricRing
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the integral closure T of the toric ring S (subalgebra generated by leading monomials of elements of input ideal I) in the basering and return an ideal listing algebra generators of T over the coefficient field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: intclToricRing(I) or intclToricRing(I, intvec grading). Note: The toric ring depends on the list of monomials given, not only the ideal. If options supp, triang, volume, or hseries are activated the function returns the input ideal and computes additional numerical invariants (accessible via showNuminvs/export). Examples show calling intclToricRing with and without grading and inspect showNuminvs output (hilbert_basis_elements, embedding_dim, integrally_closed, grading, multiplicity, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: normalToricRing
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the normalization of the toric ring S (subalgebra generated by leading monomials of elements of I) and return an ideal listing algebra generators of the normalization over the coefficient field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: normalToricRing(I) or normalToricRing(I, intvec grading). Note: depends on list of monomials; when options supp, triang, volume, or hseries activated returns input ideal and computes numerical invariants. Example shows normalToricRing producing algebra generators like y3, xy2, x2y, x3.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalToricRingFromBinomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an ideal I generated by binomials X^a - X^b representing a congruence on Z^n, compute the normalization of K[N] (monoid algebra corresponding to residue monoid M) and return a newly created polynomial ring with an ideal I listing algebra generators of the normalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: normalToricRingFromBinomials(I) or with grading. The function produces a polynomial ring of Krull dimension equal to that of K[N] whose variables represent the algebra generators; returns input ideal if certain options are activated. Example demonstrates creation of new ring S and listing I's monomial generators. See also related normaliz.lib functions ehrhartRing and intclMonIdeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: ehrhartRing
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct the Ehrhart ring of a lattice polytope defined by exponent vectors of leading monomials of I: returns ideals listing monomials representing lattice points and algebra generators of the Ehrhart ring depending on whether the last variable is auxiliary or used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: ehrhartRing(ideal I). Behavior: (i) if last ring variable not used, returns two ideals: monomials representing lattice points and algebra generators of Ehrhart ring; (ii) if last variable used, returns one ideal of monomials. Note: depends on list of monomials provided, not only the ideal. Example demonstrates returned monomials and their ordering. If options supp/triang/volume/hseries activated returns input ideal and numerical invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: intclMonIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute integral closure of a monomial ideal (via normalization of its Rees algebra) and return a list of ideals containing monomials generating the integral closure and, if appropriate, algebra generators of the normalization of the Rees algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: intclMonIdeal(I) or intclMonIdeal(I, intvec grading). Returns: (i) if last ring var not used, two ideals: first the integral closure of I (monomials), second monomials generating integral closure of Rees algebra; (ii) if last variable used, a list with one ideal (monomials generating integral closure). Note: definition of Rees algebra context given; returns input ideal if certain options activated. Example shows l[1] integral closure monomials and l[2] Rees algebra monomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: torusInvariants
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the monomial ideal listing algebra generators of the ring of invariants R^T for a torus T acting diagonally on polynomial ring, specified by an integer matrix A of exponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: torusInvariants(intmat A) or with grading. Background: T = (K^*)^r acts diagonally; matrix A with entries a_{i,j} specifies action X_j -> lambda_1^{a1j}...lambda_r^{arj} X_j. The function returns monomial ideal of invariant generators; returns input ideal if certain options activated. Example provided returning monomials y2z, xyz, x2z. See related procedures for finite groups and diagonalizable groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: finiteDiagInvariants
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute monomial ideal listing algebra generators of the ring of invariants for a finite abelian group G acting diagonally (specified by matrix U encoding action and orders of generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: finiteDiagInvariants(intmat U) or with grading. Background: rows of U are ui1 ... uin ord(gi) encoding congruence conditions for monomials; output is monomial ideal listing algebra generators of R^G. Returns input if certain options activated. Example shows many returned monomials for a 2×5 matrix input. See also diagInvariants and torusInvariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: diagInvariants
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute monomial ideal listing algebra generators of ring of invariants of a diagonalizable group D = T × G (torus × finite abelian group) acting diagonally, specified by matrices A (torus) and U (finite group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: diagInvariants(intmat A, intmat U) or with grading. Output: monomial ideal listing algebra generators. Returns input if certain options activated. Example demonstrates returned monomials for given matrices E and C. See related functions for torus and finite group invariants and intersectionValRing* functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectionValRings
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the subalgebra S = { f in R = K[X1,..,Xn] : v_i(f) >= 0 for i=1..r } determined by several discrete monomial valuations v_i given by their values on variables, returning a monomial ideal listing generators of S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: intersectionValRings(intmat V, intvec grading). Input V has rows vi(Xj). Returns monomial ideal for S. Returns input if certain options activated. Example shows returned monomials w, z, y, xw, xz, xy, x2z for a 2×4 matrix V0. See also intersectionValRingIdeals which also computes module generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectionValRingIdeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneously determine the monomial generators of S = { f : v_i(f) >= 0 } and the S-submodule M = { f : v_i(f) >= w_i } (w_i in last column) for several discrete monomial valuations, returning two ideals: generators of S and generators of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: intersectionValRingIdeals(intmat V) or with grading. Input V is matrix with r rows and n+1 columns (last column are w_i). Returns two ideals: first is monomial generators of S, second system of generators of M. Gives an error if matrix V has wrong number of columns. Example shows returned ideals for given matrix V. Returns input if certain options (supp, triang, hvect) activated.

rubrics_metrics.name: showNuminvs
rubrics_metrics.description: Print the numerical invariants computed by Normaliz operations (available after running certain normaliz.lib functions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: showNuminvs(). Purpose: prints numerical invariants such as hilbert_basis_elements, number_extreme_rays, dim_max_subspace, embedding_dim, rank, external_index, internal_index, number_support_hyperplanes, size_triangulation, sum_dets, integrally_closed, inhomogeneous, graded, degree_1_elements, grading, grading_denom, multiplicity, multiplicity_denom, hilbert_series_num, hilbert_series_denom, primary, class_group, etc. Example shows output for intclMonIdeal(I) then showNuminvs().
